title: Commutation with fixing another coordinate
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and let $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$. If $i$ and $j$ are distinct coordinates and $\omega\in\Omega$, then applying the product coordinate Laplacian in coordinate $i$ after fixing coordinate $j$ of $f$ to $\omega$ gives the same function as first applying that Laplacian and then fixing coordinate $j$ to $\omega$.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
